To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) one-third of California adolescents have handled a gun; 2) 5% of California adolescents have ever handled a firearm unsupervised, and 3) unsupervised gun-handling is associated with other adolescent health risk behaviors, and is typically shooting the gun and away from the home.
5% of California adolescents report having handled a gun without the knowledge or supervision of an adult, and that unsupervised gun use is associated with other adolescent health risk behaviors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prevalence and nature of firearm handling among adolescents.
the extent of unsupervised gun use among adolescents and the characteristics of adolescents who are involved in unsupervised gun incidents.
the prevalence of unsupervised gun carrying by adolescents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adolescents are not handling firearms unsupervised, they are not handling firearms at home, they are not shooting at targets and they are not shooting guns at friends.
unsupervised firearm handling is a significant public health issue and is associated with other risky health behaviors.
unsupervised gun use is a problem that should be addressed by health professionals, educators, law enforcement officials, parents, and others who have a stake in the well-being of children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
unsupervised firearm handling is associated with health risk behaviors and is more common than has previously been reported.

the proportion of adolescents who report that a firearm is present in their home has declined over the past decade and the proportion of adolescents reporting that they have handled guns without adult supervision has also declined.
unsupervised firearm handling is a common behavior among adolescents, and is associated with other risk behaviors and with the presence of guns in the home and with parental supervision.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vast majority (95%) of adolescents who have handled a firearm have done so with adult supervision.
unsupervised firearm handling is common among adolescents and is associated with other risky behaviors, and that it is not a benign behavior.
unsupervised gun use is not a rare occurrence and is associated with other risk behaviors.
